body.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)\), \[\tau_n(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mathbb E_P[\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\}.\] On every realized sample for which all selected Gram matrices pass and the foldwise minimizers exist, profiling the event coefficient gives \(\widehat\theta_{sk}=\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-e_0^{\top}\widehat\gamma_{sk}\); the event term then has no \(\gamma\)-dependent component, the fitted \(\widehat\gamma_{sk}\) is exactly the historical local-polynomial fit in \texttt{def:feasible-estimator}, and \(\theta_{\mathrm{FWL}}=\widehat\tau\) exactly.
body.justification: This result ties the statistical regression target to a causal level-wealth estimand and to an implementable panel coefficient.
body.gap: Goldsmith-Pinkham and Lyu identify linear return effects under factor stability; the displayed functional instead identifies compounded level wealth through a path-conditioned nonparametric transport relation.
body.consumer: Applied financial event studies obtain a declared coefficient and estimand rather than treating a generated synthetic path as an informal benchmark.
